brief: GS's Quinn tracks Nasdaq futures positioning around the Sept 15-22 rally to new all-time highs (+6.2%), driven by early success signs for Meta's AI agent (lifting Meta and semiconductor beneficiaries) and oil's tumble on UN diplomacy hopes. The option market chased upside (3-month implied vol richened, 25-delta put-call skew cheapened), but leveraged positioning arguably fell: Nasdaq 3-month funding dropped and its premium to S&P narrowed. CFTC data explains why: Non-Dealers sold $12.8bn of Nasdaq futures over five sessions, led by Hedge Funds (-$14.9bn net, including a -$15.8bn week, the largest short-selling week in 10+ years) and Non-Reportables (-$3.4bn), while Asset Managers (+$3.3bn) and Other (+$2.2bn) bought. Some hedge fund selling may have offset earlier call buying, reversing an early-September dynamic, but the funding decline suggests genuine selling occurred. Sept 22-25: higher real rates (oil resurgence) pushed Nasdaq down 0.4%, unwinding some downside positioning; funding rebounded and open interest fell. Conclusion: professional sentiment remains restrained.
